clue.text: Trojan prince is shown on standard

parts.note: par is the standard score or level
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Trojan prince appears on a battle standard or banner.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the second piece after the first, so the short word follows the standard.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Paris, son of Priam, was the Trojan prince who carried off Helen.

clue.text: Deliver a sermon, a real beauty about beginning to repent

indicators.note: about means going around, so the outer word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a peach is an informal word for a very attractive person or thing

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of repent

explanation.surface: A minister preaches on the need to repent, addressing a beautiful congregant.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach is to give a sermon, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Runs a racket in capital

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written
a bat or racket is used to hit a ball

explanation.surface: Someone operates a criminal racket in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs a racket' reads as an idiom for organised crime, but it breaks into three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco.

clue.text: Brand new floods came bringing impending disaster

parts.note: brand is an old poetic word for a sword

indicators.note: something made new is refashioned, so the following letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news report: brand-new floods have arrived, threatening catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand new' reads as one phrase meaning fresh, but it splits: the archaic word for a sword, then the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sword of Damocles, hung by a hair over a courtier in Greek legend, is an idiom for a threat of imminent catastrophe.

clue.text: Objects after shop damaged hair

indicators.note: after says the word it follows comes second, so the clue's first-written piece goes at the end

parts.note: to shop someone is to inform on them, and so is to split
ends are aims or objects

explanation.surface: Someone notices damaged hair after a visit to the salon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' wants to be a verb, but it is a noun meaning aims; 'shop' is the slang verb for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Split ends are hair tips that have frayed apart, a common sign of damaged hair.

clue.text: Prevented from participating in hobby by daughter

parts.note: a sideline is an activity pursued alongside one's main job
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A father is kept out of his hobby because his daughter has taken it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prevented from participating in hobby' reads as one phrase; 'in' is only the joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelined player is kept off the field of play, so is excluded from taking part.

clue.text: Great short piece from orchestra in a slow tempo

indicators.note: cut short, the word is clipped of its last letter

parts.note: large means great in size

indicators.note: a small piece taken from a word is here just its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of orchestra

explanation.surface: An orchestra plays a great short piece at a slow pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short piece' reads as a brief musical work; the two words belong to different operations.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the Italian musical direction for a very slow, broad pace.

clue.text: Rifleman's aid — light piece — cost's outrageous

indicators.note: an outrageous state is a wildly disordered one, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A marksman complains that a lightweight gun accessory is outrageously expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' is slang for a gun, which strengthens the shooting picture but is just fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: A telescopic sight is a magnifying scope mounted on a rifle to help the shooter aim.

clue.text: Little Edward's trapping destructive creatures — it doesn't matter

indicators.note: trapping something means closing around it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: Ned is a pet form of Edward
vermin are pests such as rats that do damage

explanation.surface: A small boy catching pests is told not to worry about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom said to dismiss something as unimportant.

clue.text: Apologetic about Church of England suggesting witchcraft

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: sorry means apologetic
CE is the standard abbreviation for Church of England

explanation.surface: The Church of England apologises over past accusations of witchcraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is magic worked through evil spirits, so is witchcraft.

clue.text: Dress up bride more elaborately

indicators.note: doing something elaborately means working it over in an intricate new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to deck out a bride even more lavishly for the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider a story is to dress it up with invented embellishments, a figurative use of decorating cloth.

clue.text: Left on account of toy boy

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
to argue over something is to argue on account of it

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned because of a young boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb about desertion, but it is just the single-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy boy is a much younger male lover of an older woman, so the general word for a romantic partner fits.

clue.text: Rotter locking Italian inside the Spanish fortress

indicators.note: something that locks another thing in holds it securely within itself

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter
IT is a standard abbreviation for Italian
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A villain imprisons an Italian inside a Spanish fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian goes inside the rotter, giving C-IT-AD, and the Spanish article follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress, typically one commanding a city.

clue.text: Outside broadcast — do watch

parts.note: OB is the broadcasting abbreviation for an outside broadcast
something that will do is something that will serve

explanation.surface: A television listing urging viewers to tune in to an outside broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do watch' reads as an emphatic command, but the two words are split between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch carefully, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Dreadful print of a dying Mozart?

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poor-quality picture of the composer Mozart on his deathbed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Mozart as an example rather than a synonym; the deathbed scene points away from his childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart composed and performed from about age five, making him the classic example of a child genius.

clue.text: One with bit of nerve to go on ahead

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just a small part, here its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of nerve
to advance is to go on or move forward

explanation.surface: A person with a little courage presses on to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in advance means done ahead of time, so the phrase is a synonym of ahead.

clue.text: Fool receiving awful clout from powerful rich type

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: prat is British slang for an idiot

indicators.note: an awful version is a badly mangled one, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An idiot gets a nasty blow from a mighty wealthy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clout' here means a blow, but it doubles as power, which suits the plutocrat picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is a person whose power derives from wealth, so a powerful rich type.

clue.text: Six feet under, or over?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally interred in a grave
second meaning: finished with for good, a matter long settled

explanation.walkthrough: 'Under, or over?' reads like a pair of opposites; in fact both words point to one phrase, literal and figurative.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a body in its grave and, by idiom, an issue that is finished and will not return.

clue.text: Traced the source of English river? I have, in the outskirts of Dartford

indicators.note: the pieces sit in the edge letters, which wrap around them
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Dartford, a town in Kent
E is the standard abbreviation for English
R is the map abbreviation for river
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have tracked an English river to its source on the edge of Dartford.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the surface into a question and answer; 'English river' is two abbreviations, not one river.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive something is to trace it back to its origin, as with a word's etymology.

clue.text: River that's cut off any number…

parts.note: to sever is to cut off
n stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: A river that's been cut off any number of times, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next in the surface only; each is solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing from Wales through western England.

clue.text: Old instrument in bar, not entirely used to make a pasta dish

indicators.note: the instrument is placed in the shortened word, which wraps around it
not entirely means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: a rail is a bar, as on a fence or towel holder
the viol is a Renaissance stringed instrument, forerunner of the violin family

explanation.surface: An antique instrument is somehow involved in making a plate of pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar loses its last letter, and the old instrument sits between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square pasta parcels with a filling, served as a dish.

clue.text: … in part of Florida, hot US state

indicators.note: a part of a phrase is a stretch of its letters, so the answer sits within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a river in a hot part of Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface steers toward Florida itself, but the answer straddles 'Florida' and 'hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state in the north-western United States.

clue.text: Animal in one, performing

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the second word wraps round the first

parts.note: taken as written
a stag is a male deer, an animal

explanation.surface: An animal is part of a performing act.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor on stage is in the middle of performing before an audience.

clue.text: Girl from the North kept in a long time

indicators.note: something kept in another is held inside it

parts.note: ages is an informal word for a long time
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A northern girl has been kept in for a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a girl's name, the standard crossword sense of 'girl'.

clue.text: Opposing female, 50, easily bribed

parts.note: V is short for versus, opposing
Ena is a woman's name, as in Ena Sharples of the British soap Coronation Street
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A hostile woman aged fifty can be bought off with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female' stands for a specific woman's name here, a crossword habit of using any girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A venal official is open to corruption and will take bribes.

clue.text: Pride in work over in island church

parts.note: Arran is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde

parts.note: a machine that goes is one that works

explanation.surface: Taking pride in one's work at a church on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed work goes inside the island, and the church abbreviation follows at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is an overbearing pride, a near synonym.

clue.text: Formal item of clothing dear? Cost's outrageous

indicators.note: something outrageous is wildly out of order, so the letters are thrown into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper balks at the price of a smart garment: expensive, and outrageously so.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress coat is a man's tailcoat worn for formal evening dress.

clue.text: Heartless teddy boy becomes a boxer

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses all its inner letters, keeping just the ends

parts.note: taken as written
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A callous young teddy boy, a 1950s British youth-culture tough, grows up to be a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: A teddy boy was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress; here 'teddy' and 'boy' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson is a former world heavyweight boxing champion, so the name is an example of a boxer.
